purpose: Round-5 study bias2, follow-up: closure trained on spatially whitened latents (local encoders, block and 8-px halo, c = 1) on the vortex, membrane and gliders worlds, with the per-channel closure configs and all hand designs again on the same data
notes: Why: in r5-bias2-005 the closure latents of the vortex world collapsed onto a box-scale mode (effective dimension 2-8 of 64, box mean 36-71% of the variance) because the closure loss normalises the pooled variance per channel; whether closure prefers a transported density (vorticity) once that collapse is closed off cannot be read from those runs. New arm (B5_ARMS=w): encoders Lw / Nw = the same local encoders L / N with the closure loss computed on latents whitened over all 64 block values (the U control's whitening, so every spatial mode has equal weight); the frozen Phi keeps per-channel whitening. 8 configs per world (Lw0, Lw8, Nw0, Nw8, and L0, L8, N0, N8 closure again as references on the same simulated data) + 2 random windows + all hand designs; everything else is the code of r5-bias2-004/005 (simulation, training settings, certification, pooling unchanged). The two minor points of the review of 004/005 are fixed (probes under timeout 120; a ctrain stopped by its time limit is reported as a deadline stop and train_done.json is written). Timing from 004/005 on an H200: vortex simulation about 250 s, 8 configs about 6-8 min, certification of about 130 halves on 13 workers about 14 min; expected 45-50 min in total, peak GPU memory 22.6 GB in 005 (so 40 GB is enough). Hard time bound: B5_JOB_HARD_S = 5100 s (660 s below the kill time of 5760 s); worlds are clipped to it. cap = 6.69 x (1.6 + 0.25) = $12.38. Public parameters, no exam secret. No network or subprocess calls after setup. CPU smoke test: job.sh end to end at tiny size (B5_TINY=1, this exact environment) from a git archive of exactly these paths at ref (affd4ecb2): exit 0, FAIL=0 for the three worlds, 403 s on CPU. ref is pinned to that tested commit; later commits changed only local analysis tools.
